label: prf:cyclotomic-dimension-synthesis-all-depths
title: Proof of cyclotomic dimension synthesis all depths
html:
Proof. Proof of cyclotomic dimension synthesis all depths

Proof — upper bound

Step 1 (count starting generators). The Galois orbit of \zeta_K yields (K - 1)/2 complex-conjugate pairs (for prime K \geq 3). Each pair gives 2 real numbers: \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^j) and \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^j). Total: K - 1 candidate generators per depth.

Step 2 (eliminate wrong-parity via Jonquière). By prop:jonquiere-cyclotomic-tate-rationality:

  • n odd: All (K - 1)/2 imaginary parts are Tate-rational (\in \pi^n \mathbb{Q}) \to collapse to 0 in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathrm{Tate}. Right-parity = Re, giving (K - 1)/2 real-part candidates.
  • n even: All (K - 1)/2 real parts are Tate-rational \to collapse to 0. Right-parity = Im, giving (K - 1)/2 imaginary-part candidates.

After this step: (K - 1)/2 candidate generators in either case.

Step 3 (apply orbit-sum relation). By prop:cyclotomic-orbit-sum-all-depths:

  • n odd: \sum_{k} \mathrm{Cl}_n(2\pi k/N) = (N^{1 - n} - 1)\,\zeta(n). This is one linear relation pulling 1 dim into the \zeta(n)-line. For n odd, \zeta(n) is not Tate-rational (Apéry: \zeta(3) \notin \pi^3 \mathbb{Q}; conjecturally \zeta(2k + 1) \notin \pi^{2k + 1} \mathbb{Q} for all k \geq 1). So this relation eliminates 1 dim from the genuinely-new content.
  • n even: \sum_{k} \mathrm{Cl}_n(2\pi k/N) = 0. Trivial — gives no relation. But also no \zeta(n) subtraction is needed: \zeta(2k) \in \pi^{2k} \mathbb{Q} is Tate-rational, hence already in the Tate-line ignored at Step 2.

Step 4 (count residual).

  • n odd: (K - 1)/2 - 1 = (K - 3)/2 genuinely-new dimensions.
  • n even: (K - 1)/2 genuinely-new dimensions (no subtraction).

\square

Lower bound — Beilinson-conditional

Borel's theorem (prop:borel-partial-resolution): for prime K, \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K) is totally complex with r_2 = (K - 1)/2.

  • n odd: \dim K_{2n - 1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = r_2 = (K - 1)/2. Modding the \zeta(n)-line gives (K - 3)/2 predicted.
  • n even: \dim K_{2n - 1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = r_1 + r_2 = (K - 1)/2. No \zeta(n) subtraction (it is already Tate). All (K - 1)/2 predicted.

Beilinson's conjecture asserts the regulator image saturates the Borel rank. Combined with the upper bound: dimensions are exactly as stated.

Depth-2 case is theorem-level (no Beilinson)

For n = 2: Bloch–Suslin (prop:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin) proves the regulator image is precisely K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} without invoking Beilinson. So:

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_{2, K} \;=\; (K - 1)/2
  \quad \text{(unconditional theorem for } n = 2 \text{)}.

This gives concrete dimensions per prime K:

K \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_{2, K} Generators
3 1 \mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi/3)
5 2 \mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi/5),\, \mathrm{Cl}_2(4\pi/5)
7 3 \mathrm{Cl}_2(2\pi/7),\, \mathrm{Cl}_2(4\pi/7),\, \mathrm{Cl}_2(6\pi/7)
11 5 5 distinct \mathrm{Cl}_2 values
13 6 6 distinct \mathrm{Cl}_2 values

Predictions at general n \geq 3

Beilinson-conditional:

Prime K n = 3 (odd, (K-3)/2) n = 4 (even, (K-1)/2) n = 5 (odd, (K-3)/2)
5 1 (confirmed) 2 1
7 2 (confirmed) 3 2
11 4 5 4
13 5 6 5

Generalises Theorem D

Theorem D (prop:cyclotomic-depth3-dimension-synthesis) gave (K - 3)/2 at n = 3. This proposition extends to:

  • All odd n: same (K - 3)/2 formula.
  • All even n: (K - 1)/2 — one MORE dimension than the odd case.

The parity difference comes from \zeta(n)'s Tate-rationality: \zeta(2k) \in \pi^{2k} \mathbb{Q} is "free" at even depths; \zeta(2k + 1) is "costly" at odd depths (subtracts one dim).
